summary.text: Kat Cammack is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 3rd District, first elected in 2020. She grew up in Colorado, worked on Rep. Ted Yoho's 2012 campaign and then served nearly a decade on his staff, and later owned a marketing firm. Her congressional office says she serves on the Agriculture and Energy and Commerce committees.

paragraphs.text: Cammack was born in Denver, Colorado, and, according to her congressional office, grew up on a cattle ranch outside Denver and took part in 4-H and local rodeo.

She earned a bachelor's degree in international relations from Metropolitan State University of Denver in 2015 and a master's degree in national defense and strategic studies from the U.S. Naval War College in 2018.
She says that after being homeless for several months she was recruited in 2011 to join Ted Yoho's congressional campaign in Florida, and that she then managed his successful 2012 campaign.
Cammack served for nearly a decade as deputy chief of staff to Rep. Yoho, according to her congressional office.
She also owned a marketing firm and describes herself as a small business owner before entering Congress.
She won the open Republican primary for Florida's 3rd District in August 2020 and the November 3, 2020 general election with 57.1% of the vote over Democrat Adam Christensen, succeeding Yoho.
Cammack was re-elected in 2022, over Danielle Hawk and Linda Brooks, and in 2024, over Tom Wells, after winning Republican primaries against Justin Waters and Alec Stevens.

In the 2025-2026 term she is assigned to the Committee on Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Communications and Technology; and Health subcommittees) and the Committee on Agriculture. Her office says she chairs the Emerging Tech Task Force and co-founded the Republican Women's Caucus in 2025.
According to her congressional office, she is married to Matt, a Gainesville Fire Rescue firefighter and paramedic, and they have a daughter.
